narrative:
Based on the information provided, the model predicts that you have a 50% chance of not passing your final year. Because this probability is well above the threshold set by the school, you are required to take additional remedial courses to support your learning and help you succeed.

The most important factor influencing this prediction is your current lack of intention to pursue higher education after graduation. In your school, every other student who is not required to take remedial courses has expressed a desire to continue their studies beyond high school. Not planning to continue your education stands out and strongly increases the likelihood that you might not pass this year, according to the model.

On the other hand, your record shows that you have not failed any classes in the past, which is a positive sign. Most students in your situation also have no previous failures, and this history actually helps reduce your risk of failing now.

Additionally, your weekend alcohol consumption is very low, which is another positive factor. Many students who are not required to take remedial courses also report low or very low alcohol use, and this healthy habit works in your favor.

Despite these strengths, the model places the most weight on your lack of plans for further education, which is why you are being asked to take remedial courses. Taking these courses is an opportunity to strengthen your skills and reconsider your future goals. Engaging fully in the support offered can help you finish the year successfully and open up more options for what comes next.
